Title: Oscillatory Characteristics of the Vocal Folds Across the Tenor Passaggio.

Journal/Date: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation (2017)

MeSH Keywords: Acoustics, Biomechanical Phenomena, Electrodiagnosis, Humans, Laryngoscopy, Male, Oscillometry, Phonation


--- ABSTRACT ---
[INTRODUCTION]: Recent research has revealed that classically trained tenors tend to constrict epilaryngeal structures when singing in and above the passaggio (ie, the frequency region where register events typically occur). These constrictions complicate visibility of vocal fold oscillatory patterns with transoral rigid high-speed video endoscopy, thus limiting the current understanding of laryngeal dynamics in the passaggio region of tenors.
[MATERIALS AND METHODS]: This investigation analyzed seven professionally trained western classical tenors using high-speed digital imaging (HSDI) at 20,000 frames per second via transnasal flexible endoscopy. The participants produced transitions (a) from modal to falsetto register and (b) from modal to stage voice above the passaggio (SVaP) during ascending pitch glides from A3 (220 Hz) to A4 (440 Hz) on vowel /i/. HSDI data were complemented by simultaneous acoustic and electroglottographic recordings.
[RESULTS]: For many subjects both transition types were associated with constrictions of the epilaryngeal structures during the pitch glide. These constrictions appeared to be more distinct for the SVaP than for falsetto. No major irregularities of vocal fold oscillations in the sense of fundamental frequency jumps were observed for either transition type. However, during the transitions, the open quotient derived from the glottal area waveform (OQGAW) increased; in falsetto, the OQGAW was greater and the electroglottographic cepstral peak prominence was lower than in SVaP.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Epilaryngeal constrictions should be considered typical for tenors singing at high fundamental frequencies. Vocal fold oscillatory patterns are changing not only for the register shift from modal to falsetto but also for the transition from modal to SVaP, indicating a need for laryngeal adjustments during these transitions.

key_findings.finding: PMID 28040341 provides direct laryngeal plus EGG/acoustic evidence that vowel condition changes passaggio oscillation. Six tenors were studied with 20,000-fps transnasal high-speed videoendoscopy, EGG, and audio across A3–A4 on [aː], [iː], and [uː]. [aː] had lower EGG sample entropy and greater phonovibrogram periodicity, indicating greater phonatory stability; for [iː] and [uː], falsetto had greater glottal-area open quotient than SVaP, whereas this difference was not large for [aː].

source_tools.relevance: Full abstract/content extraction reports instrumentation and measured oscillatory outcomes.

key_findings.finding: PMID 31668917 gives direct laryngeal, EGG, airflow, and acoustic evidence in eight professional male singers (six tenors, two baritones), using 20,000-fps transnasal high-speed videoendoscopy. SVaP transitions were more periodic and regular than modal→falsetto transitions; in four subjects, increased nasalance coincided with stabilization of open quotient at a frequency comparable to the falsetto open-quotient rise. This supports altered/stabilized glottal oscillation during the passaggio, not merely an acoustic register impression.

source_tools.relevance: Full abstract/content extraction reports subjects, modalities, and oscillation results.

key_findings.finding: PMID 33455852 directly measured six professional tenors with high-speed videoendoscopy, EGG, audio, and HSV-derived glottal-area waveforms under modal→falsetto and modal→SVaP conditions at different loudness levels. Falsetto showed a rise in open quotient; SVaP open quotient varied systematically with loudness and was lower at greater loudness. Oscillatory patterns differed across loudness conditions, but the study found no clear loudness-related difference in oscillatory stability.

source_tools.relevance: Full abstract/content extraction reports instrumentation and the open-quotient/stability findings.

key_findings.finding: The search found no qualifying tenor passaggio study centered on videokymography, inverse filtering, or airflow alone. Acoustic/EGG measures in the identified studies are generally ancillary to direct imaging; acoustic inference alone should not be treated as proof of a laryngeal register mechanism. The main acoustic/EGG-linked conclusions—periodicity, sample entropy, cepstral prominence, and open quotient—are strengthened when paired with high-speed imaging, but some EGG-versus-glottal-area disagreement occurs at high open-quotient values (>0.65).

source_tools.relevance: The videokymography-focused search returned only a non-tenor soprano paper, while the tenor studies explicitly used high-speed endoscopy with EGG/acoustics.
The vowel study explicitly reports agreement limitations between glottal-area and EGG open quotient.
